- Overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in the late part of the forecast horizon, particularly when prices are trending downward.
- Model tends to overreact to recent price spikes, leading to overshoots in the immediate next period.
- Mean reversion bias: model fails to smoothly revert to historical averages after sharp moves.
- Lagged response: model often underreacts to recent price drops, failing to anticipate downward corrections.
- Forecast horizon 1–3 days: model is overly optimistic; horizon 5–10 days: model is overly pessimistic.
- When true price drops sharply, model fails to adjust forecast downward quickly enough.
- Model overestimates volatility in the short term, leading to overconfident high forecasts.
